input: Research fertility clinics in my city

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Fertility clinics offer very different services — IVF, IUI, egg freezing, donor services, diagnostics only — and knowing which treatments are relevant narrows the research dramatically.
Whether this is for an individual, a couple, a same-sex couple, or a single parent by choice affects which clinics are relevant and what questions to prioritise.
Knowing which city determines which clinics are actually in scope, since the user said 'my city' without specifying it.
Budget and insurance coverage are major filters — some clinics accept specific insurance plans, offer financing, or have vastly different price points that may rule options in or out.
What 'done well' looks like varies: a ranked shortlist, a comparison table, a single recommendation, or a set of questions to ask clinics — determines the output format and depth.
Priorities like success rates, doctor reputation, clinic size, wait times, or proximity to home each point to different evaluation criteria and sources to consult.
Knowing how urgently this is needed and whether the user wants to compile this themselves or have a ready-to-use resource shapes how the research plan is structured and sequenced.

gold.taskTitle: Research fertility clinics in your city
gold.taskDescription: Find and evaluate fertility clinics locally to support a reproductive health decision or treatment path.

questions.title: Which specific treatments are you looking into?
questions.description: Identify the treatment type(s) relevant to the user — such as IVF, IUI, egg freezing, fertility diagnostics, or donor egg/sperm services — to narrow which clinics and services to evaluate.

questions.title: Who is this research being done for?
questions.description: Clarify whether this is for an individual, a heterosexual couple, a same-sex couple, or a single person pursuing parenthood, as this affects clinic fit and relevant questions.

questions.title: Which city should the clinic search cover?
questions.description: Confirm the specific city or metro area so the research is geographically accurate and actionable.

questions.title: What is your budget or insurance situation for treatment?
questions.description: Understand financial constraints — whether the user has fertility insurance coverage, a set out-of-pocket budget, or needs clinics with financing options — to filter clinics accordingly.

questions.title: What should the final output of this research look like?
questions.description: Determine whether the user wants a shortlist, a side-by-side comparison table, a single top recommendation, or a set of questions to bring to consultations.

questions.title: What factors matter most when evaluating a clinic?
questions.description: Identify the user's top priorities — such as success rates, doctor credentials, wait times, clinic size, patient reviews, or location proximity — to weight the research appropriately.

questions.title: How soon do you need this research completed?
questions.description: Establish the urgency and timeline so the research plan can be sequenced and paced appropriately, especially if consultations or appointments are already being considered.
